title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint
abstract: arXiv:2608.13167v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When visual evidence is occluded or chaotic, models should abstain. In this paper, we show that Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can internally distinguish when abstention is required, but fail to express it anyway. We introduce TRAPSBench, a procedurally generated video benchmark of 1,404 matched physics pairs in which a single targeted change renders the outcome undeterminable from the visual evidence. Furthermore, we introduce Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score (PECS), a new robust metric that requires models to both answer correctly when the outcome is knowable, and abstain when the outcome is not. Across 16 VLMs spanning five families, spontaneous restraint is poor: the best PECS is 0.292. The bottleneck is expression, not perception: linear probes decode answerability from hidden states at up to 0.91 AUROC across physics domains; steering a single-layer void direction causally induces or suppresses abstention. translated_title: TRAPSBench：视觉语言模型能够编码但未能表达认知克制
translated_abstract: 当视觉证据被遮挡或混乱时，模型应该选择弃权。在本文中，我们表明视觉语言模型（VLMs）在内部能够区分何时需要弃权，但未能表达出来。我们引入了TRAPSBench，一个程序生成的视频基准，包含1,404对匹配的物理场景，其中单个有针对性的变化使得结果无法从视觉证据中确定。此外，我们引入了惩罚性认知校准分数（PECS），这是一种新的稳健指标，要求模型在结果可知时正确回答，在结果不可知时弃权。在跨越五个家族的16个VLM中，自发克制表现不佳：最佳PECS为0.292。瓶颈在于表达而非感知：线性探针在物理域中从隐藏状态解码可回答性的AUROC最高可达0.91；引导单层空隙方向可以因果性地诱导或抑制弃权。我们的结果复现了这些发现。
tldr: 视觉语言模型能够内部识别何时应弃权，但无法表达这种认知克制，瓶颈在于表达而非感知。
en_tdlr: Vision-language models can internally identify when to abstain but fail to express it, with the bottleneck being expression rather than perception.
